cards.runner_up: Rust stops enumerating halo phases (it parses them only to compute phase != idle): the producer declares visibility, so a phase is a TS-only change instead of a three-language hand-list pinned by regex tests.
cards.body:
## Summary
Her two mirrors disagree on when she is speaking. The face holds 'speaking' until the player has played the last sample of her line; the halo drops it the moment the store hears voice.stopped, which synthesis sends ahead of playback. So at the end of a spoken reply the screen edges go dark (or violet, or pink if a card landed) and the level stops following her voice while she is still audibly talking, and the caption's 4 s linger starts early. The fix is structural: the phase-with-tail rule moves out of face-signal's private phaseOf into one reducer beside haloPhase, and both producers read it.

## Description
halo-signal.ts gains createPresence({ sounding }): a tiny stateful reducer that remembers the last generation it saw playing and returns haloPhase(voice, run, cards), except that a non-listening, non-speaking phase reads 'speaking' while that generation still sounds (the exact rule at face-signal.ts:162). The halo producer adds generation to HaloInputs and sounding to HaloDeps (liveHaloDeps wires playbackSounding, read-only), and computes phase through the reducer in both signalOf's caller and emit. Because the phase stays 'speaking' through the tail, the existing level loop keeps running, so each 34 ms tick re-evaluates the reducer and the loop stops itself the tick the tail ends: no new timer, rest still free. The caption needs nothing: a null caption erases nothing in the overlay, so her last line stays up through the tail and its linger starts when she really stops. face-signal.ts replaces its private spoken/phaseOf with the shared reducer, so the rule exists once (the face's own tail test is the guard). Technique: status-vocabulary/vocabulary-chain-integrity (one authority, derivations not forks); motion/continuity-across-change.

## Flow
- She answers aloud; the daemon's voice.stopped lands while the player still has the last sentence queued
- Today: halo edges fade to idle, the level freezes, the face keeps talking - two renderings of her contradict each other
- After: the halo stays on speaking, edges breathing with her real playback level, until the last sample; then idle (or gate if a card waits)
- A press during the tail still wins (listening first)

## Expected impact
Every spoken reply whose audio outlasts synthesis (any multi-sentence reply) ends with the halo in step with her voice instead of going dark mid-word, and the halo and her face can no longer disagree on her phase because they read one reducer. The parity case pins it so a future rule lands in both or neither.

## Evaluation
Claim: the halo and the face derive her phase from one reducer, and the halo follows audible playback
Before: 0 of 6 non-guard acceptance cases pass (the halo has no generation or sounding input; halo.ts:173)
After: 6 of 6, guards [6] and [7] green before and after
Method: gate - the acceptance cases under vitest with fake deps and fake timers
Result: better
Gate: none
cards.evidence: face-signal.ts:158-163: `const phaseOf = (inputs) => { if (inputs.generation !== null) spoken = inputs.generation; const phase = haloPhase(inputs.voice, inputs.run, inputs.cards); if (phase !== "listening" && phase !== "speaking" && spoken !== null && deps.sounding(spoken)) return "speaking"; return phase; }`. halo.ts:173: `const phase = override?.phase ?? haloPhase(inputs.voice, inputs.run, inputs.cards);` and HaloInputs (halo.ts:40-51) carries no generation. voice.ts:361-366 sets `generation: null, speakingText: "", phase: get().phase === "speaking" ? "idle" : get().phase` on voice.stopped. face-signal.test.ts:174 already pins the face's tail; no halo test mentions sounding (grep: 0 hits in lib/halo.test.ts).

cards.body:
## Summary
Hold the chord, speak, let go - and if the turn fails (released too fast, a silent microphone, no words, a daemon error, the voice socket dropping), the halo simply fades to idle, exactly as it does after a good answer. Her window is put away, so the person gets nothing: they cannot tell 'she is done' from 'she never heard me'. The voice and run stores already know why, in sentences (endedBecause, plainFailure). This card gives the halo a sixth phase, 'trouble': an amber edge for a moment with her plain reason as the caption, on every turn the person started that ended without an answer.

## Description
Vocabulary (one change, every layer - status-vocabulary/vocabulary-evolution-checklist): HALO_PHASES gains 'trouble'; the Rust mirror gains the variant and arm (wants_visible needs nothing: non-idle shows); model.ts HOLDS gains it so the caption is held through it and lingers after; halo.css adds --halo-trouble pinned to --status-warning, a still edge (no travel, no breathe), so reduced motion keeps the hue and the caption (motion/content-bearing-degradation); haloPhase keeps returning the five store phases (typed Exclude) so FacePhase is untouched. Producer: HaloInputs adds voiceReason, runError and the engine name; emit keeps the previous inputs and raises trouble only on an edge - an active turn (voice listening/thinking/speaking or run running/acting) followed by a non-empty voice reason or run error. troubleLine(inputs) is pure: ended-utterance sentences capitalised as they are, run errors through plainFailure, a voice turn.error through plainFailure on its reason prefix, a socket close as one fixed sentence; never the raw detail. A TROUBLE_MS timer (about 2.5 s) returns to the store phase (idle or gate), cancelled by any newer active phase. Precedence: listening > speaking > thinking > trouble > gate > idle; cards ride every frame. The rehearsal and demo script gain one trouble step so the look can be tuned without a backend.

## Flow
- Person holds the chord with her window put away, says nothing useful, lets go
- Today: pale cyan -> violet -> fade; nothing says why
- After: pale cyan -> violet -> amber edge with 'Your microphone sounded silent (-62 dB), check the input in Voice settings' -> lingers -> fades
- A typed run that times out while she is hidden shows 'That took too long, so Athena stopped it.' the same way
- A press during the amber moment starts listening at once

## Expected impact
Every failed voice or run turn while her window is away stops being silent: the person learns in the moment whether to speak again, check the microphone or open Setup, without summoning her window. The halo moves from reporting four happy states to reporting the one state the person must act on differently.

## Evaluation
Claim: a turn the person started that ends in failure shows a trouble phase with a plain reason; nothing else changes
Before: 0 of 6 non-guard acceptance cases pass (no producer path reads voice.reason or run.error; halo.ts:79)
After: 6 of 6, guards [2] and [6] green before and after
Method: gate - the acceptance cases (vitest, fake deps and timers) plus the Rust phase test
Result: better
Gate: none
